```python
import copy

import pytest

from your_module import matrix_transpose


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "matrix, expected",
    [
        pytest.param([], [], id="empty-matrix"),
        pytest.param([[1, 2], [3, 4]], [[1, 3], [2, 4]], id="square-matrix"),
        pytest.param(
            [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]],
            [[1, 4], [2, 5], [3, 6]],
            id="rectangular-wide-matrix",
        ),
        pytest.param(
            [[1, 2], [3, 4], [5, 6]],
            [[1, 3, 5], [2, 4, 6]],
            id="rectangular-tall-matrix",
        ),
        pytest.param([[1, 2, 3]], [[1], [2], [3]], id="single-row"),
        pytest.param([[1], [2], [3]], [[1, 2, 3]], id="single-column"),
        pytest.param(
            [[1, "a"], [None, True]],
            [[1, None], ["a", True]],
            id="mixed-values",
        ),
        pytest.param([[]], [], id="one-empty-row"),
        pytest.param([[], []], [], id="multiple-empty-rows"),
    ],
)
def test_matrix_transpose_valid_inputs(matrix, expected):
    assert matrix_transpose(matrix) == expected


def test_matrix_transpose_does_not_mutate_input():
    matrix = [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5, 6]]
    original = copy.deepcopy(matrix)

    result = matrix_transpose(matrix)

    assert result == [[1, 4], [2, 5], [3, 6]]
    assert matrix == original


def test_matrix_transpose_empty_first_row_ignores_later_rows_current_behavior():
    # Current implementation uses len(matrix[0]), so later values are ignored
    # when the first row is empty.
    assert matrix_transpose([[], [1, 2]]) == []


def test_matrix_transpose_ragged_matrix_longer_later_rows_are_truncated_current_behavior():
    # Current implementation only iterates over indexes present in the first row.
    assert matrix_transpose([[1], [2, 3], [4, 5]]) == [[1, 2, 4]]


@pytest.mark.parametrize(
    "matrix, expected_exception",
    [
        pytest.param(
            [[1, 2, 3], [4, 5]],
            IndexError,
            id="later-row-shorter-than-first",
        ),
        pytest.param(
            [[1, 2], []],
            IndexError,
            id="later-row-empty",
        ),
        pytest.param(
            [1, 2, 3],
            TypeError,
            id="flat-list-not-list-of-rows",
        ),
        pytest.param(
            [[1, 2], 3],
            TypeError,
            id="later-row-not-subscriptable",
        ),
    ],
)
def test_matrix_transpose_invalid_inputs_raise(matrix, expected_exception):
    with pytest.raises(expected_exception):
        matrix_transpose(matrix)
```

The two tests marked `current_behavior` document quirks of the current implementation for ragged matrices. If ragged matrices should always be invalid, the function should be updated to validate row lengths explicitly.
